key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:CF96
name: compute_base_relative_address
description: Returns an address formed by adding a fixed negative offset to the A4 base register, giving a pointer to a slot in the global data area. The routine has one caller and makes no calls.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:CFB0
name: clear_table_and_open_libraries
description: Zeroes a long block of longwords, records the exec library base in a global, and checks a flag bit in a library structure before calling a library vector. It then opens a library through exec, calling a second vector when the open fails, and refers to the dos.library name.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D022
name: stub_return_only
description: Routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use; it does no work.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D02A
name: allocate_and_fill_file_record
description: Allocates a block sized from a stored index multiplied by six, sets its header fields and writes a four-character tag into it. It then calls the dos wrappers for current directory, input, output and open, stores their results in the block, and returns through a library vector.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D164
name: split_command_line_arguments
description: Splits a text buffer into whitespace-separated tokens, keeping spaces inside double quotes and treating a doubled quote as one quote character. It counts the tokens, requests a pointer table with one entry per token plus a terminator, and stores each token's start address in it.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D30A
name: copy_string_pad_zeros
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination buffer until a zero byte is copied or the count runs out, then writes zero bytes over the rest of the count. It returns the destination pointer.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D32C
name: append_string_capped
description: Moves to the end of the destination string and copies the source after it, stopping at a zero byte or after a fixed maximum length. If the limit is reached before the source ends, it writes a terminating zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D332
name: append_string_with_count
description: Scans to the end of the destination string, then copies the source onto it until a zero byte or until the count argument runs out. When the count expires before the source ends, it writes a terminating zero after the copied text.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D356
name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination buffer until a zero byte is copied, including the terminator. It returns the original destination pointer.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D366
name: multiply_low_32_bit_product
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values by summing the cross products of their 16-bit halves, so only the low 32 bits of the product are computed. It returns that product in the upper result word and the second operand in the lower word.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D38A
name: load_icon_library_for_window
description: Opens a library by a global name and, if that succeeds, uses a value from the caller's structure to open a second resource. It stores the resulting pointers in fields of the first structure, then calls a library vector to close the library and clears a global handle. The referenced text names a window and icon.library.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D43C
name: format_into_buffer
description: Stores a destination pointer in a global, runs a formatting routine that emits characters through the byte-writing callback, then writes a terminating zero at the destination. It returns the formatter's result.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D43E
name: format_into_buffer_short
description: Stores a destination pointer in a global, runs a formatting routine that emits characters through the byte-writing callback, then writes a terminating zero at the destination. It returns the formatter's count as a 16-bit value.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D46E
name: write_byte_advance_cursor
description: Writes the low byte of its argument to the location held in a global cursor pointer, advances that cursor by one, and returns the byte. It works as a per-character output callback.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D48A
name: forward_format_to_callback
description: Passes a format string and its stack arguments to the formatter, using the byte-writing callback as the output routine. It returns nothing.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D4A6
name: invoke_two_subroutines
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The routine has 48 instructions, is called by one routine, and calls two routines; nothing more can be stated from the evidence.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D534
name: format_string_to_output
description: Walks a format string, sending literal characters through an output callback and handling conversion specifiers with flags, width, precision and length modifiers. It supports character, string, decimal, octal, unsigned and sixteen-based integer conversions, and returns the number of characters written or -1 when the callback fails.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D84E
name: apply_operand_sign_to_result
description: Sets a sign flag from the signs of its two operands, calls another routine, and negates that routine's result when the flag is set. It returns the result in the upper word with the second operand in the lower word; the pseudo-code does not show what the called routine computes.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D876
name: negate_when_first_negative
description: Calls another routine, then negates the value it leaves in the D1 register when the first operand is negative. It returns that value in the upper word with the second operand in the lower word.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D890
name: call_and_return_concatenated
description: Calls another routine and returns a 64-bit value whose upper half is the value that routine left in the D1 register and whose lower half is the D1 value from before the call.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D89C
name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one routine and then returns, with no other work in the body. The pseudo-code does not show whether the callee is this same routine.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D8A6
name: perform_32bit_division
description: Divides the 32-bit dividend in D0 by the divisor in D1 and returns the quotient in the upper half and the remainder in the lower half of a 64-bit result. For divisors wider than 16 bits it uses a bit-by-bit shift-and-subtract loop; otherwise it uses 16-bit division.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D8F6
name: compute_string_length
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte string to its terminator and returns the number of bytes before it. It does not write to memory.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D908
name: trampoline_call_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns, passing its own stack arguments along. It is referenced by its address, so it can be used as a callback.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D91E
name: invoke_three_subroutines
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The routine has 21 instructions, is referenced by its address and called by two routines, and calls three routines; nothing more can be stated from the evidence.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D95E
name: stub_return_only
description: Pseudo-code is only a return, so the body does no work. The listing reports one call that the pseudo-code does not show.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D960
name: sequence_two_subroutine_calls
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The routine has 15 instructions, is referenced by its address and called by two routines, and calls two routines; nothing more can be stated from the evidence.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D98A
name: write_global_byte_advance_cursor
description: Stores a byte from a fixed global location into the address held in a cursor register, advances that cursor by one, and returns the byte. It is referenced by its address and works as a per-character output routine.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D99C
name: call_routine_for_each_record
description: Walks an array of 22-byte records from a start address up to a fixed end address, calling another routine with each record's address.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D9C4
name: release_record_resources
description: Returns a minus-one value for a null pointer. Otherwise, when the record's flag byte is set, it calls routines for the resources flagged there, ORs their results together, and clears the record's three words and flag byte.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:D9E0
name: release_record_without_check
description: Applies the same flag-driven calls and field clearing as the null-checked cleanup routine to the record in address register A2, without a null check. It returns the OR of the call results.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DA4A
name: put_byte_into_buffer
description: Writes one byte into a buffered output record and returns it, or returns a minus-one failure value when the record's error flag is set. A minus-one argument resets the buffer and returns zero, and an empty buffer gets its start and end pointers set before the byte is stored.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DA70
name: put_global_byte_into_buffer
description: Writes a byte taken from a fixed global location into a buffered output record and returns the stored value. It follows the same flow as the buffered byte writer, with a minus-one failure value when the error flag is set.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DAA8
name: write_global_byte_size_check
description: Writes a byte from a fixed global location into an output record. When the record's size field is one, it passes the byte to another routine and returns the stored value or sets an error flag; otherwise it sets the buffer pointers and stores the byte directly.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DAC0
name: write_global_byte_to_record
description: Writes a byte from a fixed global location into the record's buffer, or passes it to another routine when the size field is one. If that routine fails, it sets an error flag and returns a minus-one value.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DB00
name: write_global_byte_fast_path
description: Resets the record's pointer from its base field, sets its end pointer from the size field and marks the buffer active. It then stores a byte from a fixed global location at the cursor and returns it.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DB2C
name: find_free_record_slot
description: Scans an array of 22-byte records for the first one whose flag byte is clear, zeroes its three words and returns its address. It returns a null pointer when every record is in use.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DB54
name: find_free_record_from_pointer
description: Starts from the record in address register A2 and checks one 22-byte record at a time for a clear flag byte. When it finds one, it zeroes that record's three words and returns its address; otherwise it returns a null pointer.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DB56
name: clear_record_header_words
description: Zeroes three consecutive longwords starting at the address held in A2.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DB64
name: initialize_record_buffer
description: Calls another routine to obtain a buffer pointer. When the result is zero, it sets a size field to one and points the record's buffer at an area inside the record; otherwise it sets a larger size field, flags the record, stores the returned pointer, and sets a further flag when a second routine returns nonzero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DB96
name: initialize_record_from_global
description: Sets a large size field in the record, sets a flag bit, and stores a pointer taken from a global slot into the record. It then calls another routine and sets a further flag bit when that call returns nonzero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DBC2
name: process_all_list_records
description: Walks a singly linked list of records from a global head pointer, calling another routine on each record with a size taken from the record's second longword plus eight. It then clears the head pointer and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DBD0
name: process_record_list_from_pointer
description: Walks a singly linked list of records starting at the address held in A2, calling another routine on each record with a size taken from its second longword plus eight. It then clears a global head pointer and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DBF4
name: allocate_record_and_link
description: Requests a block of the argument plus eight bytes through a library call. On success it pushes the block onto a global linked list, stores the argument in its second longword and returns the address past the two-longword header; on failure it returns a null pointer.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC20
name: link_record_into_list
description: Pushes the record at the address in A2 onto the front of a global linked list, stores a value from a fixed slot in the A5 base in its second longword, and returns the address past the two-longword header.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC34
name: forward_low_word_argument
description: Forwards the low 16-bit word of its 32-bit argument to another routine and then returns. It performs no other operations.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC48
name: unlink_record_from_list
description: Searches the global linked list for the record whose data address is the argument minus eight. When it finds the record, it unlinks it, passes it to another routine with a size taken from its second longword plus eight, and returns zero; if the record is not in the list it returns a minus-one value.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC58
name: unlink_record_matching_global
description: Searches a linked list starting at the address in A2 for the record whose data address matches a fixed global slot. When it finds the record, it unlinks it, passes it to another routine with its size, and returns zero; if no record matches it returns a minus-one value.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC74
name: unlink_record_from_predecessor
description: Removes the record at A2 from a linked list by pointing its predecessor at the record's next pointer, or updates the global head when the record is first. It then calls another routine and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC7C
name: remove_list_head_record
description: Sets the global list head to the next pointer of the record in A2, calls another routine, and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DC94
name: check_table_entry_active
description: Checks a record index against a bound held in a global and returns minus one, with an error code of two stored in a global, when the index is negative, too large, or points at an empty table entry. Otherwise it calls another routine with the table entry and returns one or zero depending on that result.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DCCA
name: check_handle_interactive
description: Looks up a six-byte table entry using the index stored at a fixed offset in the A5 base, passes its value through another routine that wraps the dos IsInteractive call, and returns whether the result is nonzero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DCE8
name: stub_return_zero
description: Pseudo-code only returns zero, with no calls or memory access in the body.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DCEC
name: delete_file_store_error
description: Calls a routine with its argument, which the listing associates with the dos DeleteFile wrapper. When that call returns zero, it reads the dos error code through the IoErr wrapper, stores it in a global error slot and returns minus one; otherwise it returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DD0C
name: stub_return_zero
description: Pseudo-code only returns zero, with no calls or memory access in the body.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DD10
name: invoke_two_unnamed_routines
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The routine has 19 instructions, is referenced by its address and called by five routines, and calls two routines; nothing more can be stated from the evidence.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DD4A
name: dos_transfer_with_error_check
description: Returns minus one and sets an error code of five when the record's access bits are clear. Otherwise it calls another routine with a record pointer, a value from the A5 base and a word; when that returns minus one, it reads the dos error code and stores it in a global error slot.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DD5E
name: write_record_store_error
description: Calls a routine with a record pointer, a value from the A5 base and a word, which the listing associates with the dos Write wrapper. When that call returns minus one, it reads the dos error code, stores it in a global error slot and returns minus one.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DD8A
name: stub_return_only
description: Pseudo-code is only a return, so the body does no work.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DD8E
name: check_signal_bit_flag
description: Calls a library routine with a zero value and a single-bit mask, then tests that bit in the result. When the bit is set and a global flag is zero it returns the library result; when the flag is nonzero it calls another routine. It returns zero when the bit is clear.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DDB6
name: call_then_return_zero
description: Calls one routine and returns zero. The listing reports two calls, but the pseudo-code shows only one.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DDBE
name: call_fixed_address_then_write
description: Calls a routine with a fixed address and the value four, passes its result to a second routine, then calls a library vector and returns. The listing associates the calls with the dos Output and Write wrappers.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DDEA
name: run_hook_then_call
description: Calls a hook through a global pointer when that pointer is set, then calls another routine and returns.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DE08
name: release_table_and_resources
description: Calls another routine on each six-byte table entry, releases the table block, and invokes an optional hook. It then releases three further stored pointers when they are set, calls a library vector when a flag bit is set, and finishes with a short sequence of calls on stored pointers.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DE22
name: release_table_entries_supervised
description: Calls another routine on each six-byte table entry, releases the table block, invokes an optional hook and releases three further stored pointers. It then performs the final call sequence; the listing references exec.Supervisor and a library vector.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DEA2
name: finish_buffer_release_sequence
description: When the secondary pointer is clear and the primary pointer is set, calls another routine with the stored pointer and a size from the stored count, then again with the second stored pointer and a size of the count plus one, times four. Otherwise it calls another routine and then releases the secondary pointer.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DED8
name: call_library_then_return_value
description: Calls one library routine with no argument, then calls a second library routine with a stored pointer, and returns a longword taken from the A5 base.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DEF6
name: clear_table_entry_by_index
description: Validates a six-byte table index against a count held in a global. When the index is negative, too large or refers to an empty entry, it stores error code two and returns minus one. Otherwise it calls another routine with the entry's pointer unless a flag bit is set, clears the entry and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DF2C
name: close_handle_clear_slot
description: Calls a routine that the listing associates with the dos Close wrapper, passing the handle stored at the address in A2, unless a flag bit is set. It then clears that stored handle to zero and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DF44
name: call_dos_close_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the Close function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DF78
name: call_dos_examine_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the Examine function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DFA6
name: call_dos_lock_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the Lock function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DFB8
name: call_dos_open_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the Open function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DFD2
name: call_dos_read_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the Read function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DFE4
name: call_dos_unlock_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the UnLock function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:DFF4
name: call_dos_write_vector
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from the dos library base, which the listing identifies as the Write function. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the result is returned.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E044
name: forward_library_vector_call
description: Jumps through a library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot. The listing does not identify which library function this is.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E054
name: allocate_record_with_fields
description: Calls a routine with a minus-one argument and returns zero when the result is minus one. Otherwise it allocates a 34-byte block through a library call, stores the argument and a byte in its fields, sets a count of four, and stores the result of a second routine. It then passes the block to another routine, and on allocation failure passes the first result to another routine and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E07A
name: allocate_record_from_globals
description: Allocates a 34-byte block through a library call and fills its fields from fixed global slots, storing the result of a second routine in it. It then passes the block to another routine; on allocation failure it calls another routine and returns zero.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E09C
name: fill_record_from_globals
description: Fills the record in address register A2 from fixed global slots, using the same field layout as the allocation routine, and stores the result of a second routine in it. It then passes the record to another routine.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E0D2
name: pass_record_field_address
description: Calls another routine with the address of a field fourteen bytes into the record in address register A2, then returns.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E0E0
name: release_record_block
description: Clears the record's marker byte and two longword sentinels, calls another routine on the record's byte field when its pointer field is set, and then frees the record block through a library call.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E13E
name: call_with_constant_48
description: Calls another routine with the input parameter and the fixed value 48, then returns.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E154
name: forward_pointer_argument
description: Passes its pointer argument to another routine and returns without other work.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E166
name: allocate_tagged_block
description: Returns zero when the first argument is zero. Otherwise it allocates a block of the requested size through a library call, sets a type byte of five, stores the first argument and the size in the block, and returns the block address, or zero when the allocation fails.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E1AA
name: free_tagged_block
description: Returns zero for a null pointer. Otherwise it marks the block's type byte and two longword fields as unused, then frees the block through a library call using the size word stored in it, and returns that call's result.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E1E6
name: forward_library_vector_198
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the listing identifies the vector as the one at minus 198.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E20E
name: forward_library_vector_294
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the listing identifies the vector as the one at minus 294.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E21E
name: forward_library_vector_132
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the listing identifies the vector as the one at minus 132.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E22A
name: forward_library_vector_210
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the listing identifies the vector as the one at minus 210.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E256
name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Stores the address of its pointer argument into the memory it points to, adds four to that stored value, clears the next longword in the block and stores the original pointer value in the longword after it.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E27E
name: forward_library_vector_552
description: Jumps through the library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot. The indirect jump is treated as a call and the listing identifies the vector as the one at minus 552.

key: star wars (1987)(domark)/Star Wars (1987)(Domark).adf:starwars:0:E314
name: setup_disk_track_dma
description: Sets up the floppy disk controller for a track transfer: it disables interrupts around a timing loop, writes a sync word and the buffer address and length to the disk registers, and enables interrupts again. It allocates its buffer through a library call, and on allocation failure it enters a loop that jumps through an address the decompiler could not resolve. It is called by find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:C/Type:0:0136
name: copy_sixteen_longs_and_call
description: When the stack argument is non-null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in the structure held in address register A2 into that argument, then calls a routine through a function pointer. The listing identifies that routine as find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:C/Wait:0:0000
name: run_wait_command_setup
description: Program entry for the Wait command. It calls a routine through a function pointer, walks a linked list of entries to find the largest value in one field, and calls find_max_and_prepare_buffer. It then fills a structure from a stack buffer and returns zero when that succeeds, or minus one on failure.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:C/Wait:0:0136
name: copy_sixteen_longs_and_call
description: When the stack argument is non-null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in the structure held in address register A2 into that argument, then calls a routine through a function pointer. The listing identifies that routine as find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:L/Disk-Validator:0:0000
name: run_disk_validator_entry
description: Program entry for the Disk-Validator command. The visible code writes a decimal count into a text buffer, initialises a table of minus-one entries, and builds bit masks over a range of longword indices through calls via a function pointer. The pseudo-code is truncated in the listing, so only these parts are described.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:0000
name: clear_block_and_call_setup
description: Program entry for FMAIN. It clears a large block of longwords starting at a computed offset, stores a register value and a global value in fixed slots, and then calls one other routine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:016E
name: initialize_graphics_and_devices
description: Opens graphics.library and layers.library, uses the Amber font at size nine, and refers to trackdisk.device. It allocates buffers and sets up list headers and structures; it returns zero on success or a failure code identifying the step that failed. The pseudo-code is truncated at the end, so the later steps are not described.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:08BA
name: release_flagged_resources
description: Frees each resource whose flag bit is set in the status bytes by calling a memory-release vector with a fixed size for that resource. It then calls library vectors to tear down the remaining structures, clears a flag word and returns.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:0B36
name: index_length_prefixed_blocks
description: Allocates a block through a library call, then walks a block of length-prefixed records: each longword gives the size of the record that follows it. The routine stores the start address and size of each of six records in two tables.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:0BCC
name: update_map_tile_from_table
description: Probes the requested position and nearby offsets with a query routine, then searches a 17-entry table for a row matching the tile bytes and an argument flag. On a match it writes replacement tile values into the map buffer, sets a global flag and returns one; otherwise it returns zero. The referenced text 'It opened.' and 'It's locked.' is the only message in the routine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:0EEE
name: setup_display_state
description: Large setup routine that initialises the display and graphics state by calling many library vectors and routines, including buffer and screen setup. The listing refers to the text 'No Arrows!', 'hiscreen' and 'page0', and is truncated early in its body, so only its opening steps are described.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5716
name: update_position_and_advance_y
description: Updates the stored x and y coordinates by the difference from their previous values and stores the new position. When the third argument is nonzero it sets a value derived from those coordinates, then advances the stored y coordinate while a query routine returns nonzero.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:57FA
name: update_region_code_from_position
description: Looks up the current position in a table of rectangular regions with twelve-byte entries, and updates a stored region code when it changes. It calls routines for certain codes, including a special case for one code when a flag is set, and then sets coordinates and runs a short loop depending on the code. The listing is only partly interpreted.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5B1C
name: update_code_from_lookup_table
description: Adds a value from a helper call to a stored byte and derives a table index from a stored word. When the table value differs from the stored code, it stores the new code, sets a counter to three, calls a routine with the code, and sets a flag.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5B9E
name: compute_offset_target_coordinates
description: Computes two target coordinates from the stored position and two helper results, adding a fixed offset of 150 to the second result, then passes them to two routines and stores the results in the stored target fields.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5BF0
name: place_entry_near_position
description: Tries up to fifteen nearby positions, offset by values from a routine, until a query routine reports an acceptable spot. It then stores that position and derived type and flag bytes into the 22-byte record at the given index, returning one on success and zero when no spot was accepted.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5DE0
name: reset_expired_entry_state
description: Resets a 22-byte record when its counter is not positive and its kind is not one of two reserved values, setting its state bytes and counter. It then applies a kind-specific adjustment and calls a routine; when the argument is zero it calls another routine and adjusts a global, otherwise it increments a global counter.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5EAA
name: set_mode_and_reset_state
description: Sets a mode byte to six when the argument is ten and to five otherwise. When the stored code differs from the argument, it updates a stored pointer and calls two routines with the new code, then sets a position pair from table lookups, clears several flag bytes, sets a counter of fifty and stores the argument.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:5F88
name: initialize_scene_state
description: Initialises a large block of state fields in the game data. When the argument is nonzero it calls a sequence of routines and library vectors for drawing and loading. The listing is truncated after the initial state setup, so the later steps are not described.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:637C
name: set_layout_fields_from_argument
description: Calls two routines for values, then sets several layout fields from the argument and those values, using offsets from 160 and 100 and doubled values. It calls a library vector with computed coordinates and then calls another routine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:642C
name: call_group_from_index_table
description: Chooses an index into a table of four-longword groups according to a state value and a position range, then calls a routine with the four values of that group. It uses one routine when the first argument is zero and another routine otherwise.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:6534
name: update_state_from_position_bits
description: Derives a small state value from masked position bits and, when it changes, stores it and calls a routine. It recalculates two offset fields from the state when a check passes or a counter is high, then calls a routine with two stored values.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:6660
name: swap_double_buffer_pointers
description: Swaps two global buffer pointers, copies the first longword of the new buffer into one field and its second longword into another, then calls three library vectors on the fixed structures and restores the second longword.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:66B6
name: open_input_device
description: Creates a message port and an input request block, then opens input.device with that request. When the open succeeds it sets fields, calls a library routine and returns one. When the open fails it returns zero, and if the request block cannot be created it releases the port and returns zero.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:6766
name: close_input_device
description: Sets the input request's command field to ten, calls library vectors to perform the request and close the device, and then releases the message port.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:67AC
name: render_flagged_entries
description: Calls a routine for each flagged entry in a state-specific table, up to twelve entries. It then fills up to twelve slots with a value chosen by parity from two constants and calls drawing vectors at computed positions.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:68CA
name: draw_entry_cell_for_state
description: Chooses a cell value from a lookup that depends on the current state, then draws it at a position derived from the record, using a horizontal offset chosen by a parity bit. Library vectors perform the placement.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:6A66
name: handle_state_event_switch
description: Dispatches on the current state value with a switch. The visible branches handle event codes five, six and eight for the first state, calling routines that draw rows and process entries. The listing is truncated in its first case, so the remaining states are not described.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:7ED2
name: probe_until_code_five
description: Calls another routine and queries a function at the stored coordinates up to twenty-five times, stopping when it returns five. If five is never returned, it calls a function with one and the coordinates, then calls another routine with five.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:7F18
name: notify_coordinates_and_call_five
description: Calls a function with one and the stored coordinates, then calls another routine with the value five.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:7F40
name: set_state_when_flag_clear
description: When bit one of a flag byte is clear, stores its argument into a state word, clears a second flag byte and calls another routine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:7F60
name: load_byte_lookup_tables
description: Fills several small byte tables by calling a lookup routine with computed indices. Some entries are eight by default, and one entry becomes ten when a stored value exceeds two.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:800E
name: wait_until_counter_reaches_ten
description: Calls another routine repeatedly while a stored counter is below ten, and returns once the counter reaches ten.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8022
name: refresh_cached_entry_resources
description: When a counter is below ten, compares an entry's stored fields with cached values. If one changed, it calls a resource routine to update the entry and copies the new value into the cache. Otherwise it clears status fields on seven records; in either case it then saves the counter and sets it to ten.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:82A0
name: call_indexed_entry_half_size
description: When a flag bit is set, calls a routine with the pointer and half the size of the table entry chosen by the argument, together with the second argument.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:82E0
name: free_fixed_buffers
description: Frees three fixed 35-byte buffers and one 60-byte buffer through a library call, and sets a pointer from a table entry chosen by an index.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8334
name: store_argument_in_block
description: Stores its stack argument as a longword at offset four of the block in address register A1, then returns.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:833A
name: process_event_list_entries
description: Walks a linked list of event entries. Type-one entries are written as bytes into a 128-entry ring buffer in the block, and type-two entries update their flag bits. Each entry's position is clamped to fixed bounds and stored, and a callback is called when its callback pointer is set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8390
name: walk_event_list_type_two
description: Variant entry of the event-list walker that starts at the type-two check. It shares the same position clamping, ring-buffer writes and callback handling as the neighbouring walker.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:83BC
name: process_event_list_with_callback
description: Walks the same kind of event list as its neighbours, clamping positions and writing type-one entries to the ring buffer. It calls a library vector at a fixed offset whenever an entry's callback pointer is set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:84EA
name: read_next_ring_buffer_byte
description: Returns the next byte from a 128-entry ring buffer when the read and write indices differ, and advances the read index modulo 128. It returns zero when the buffer is empty.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8514
name: next_pseudo_random_value
description: Advances a 16-bit state word with a multiply-and-add step, stores the new state and returns a value formed from its bits.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:852C
name: mask_result_with_argument
description: Calls another routine for a value and returns its bitwise AND with the argument.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8534
name: mask_result_low_bit
description: Calls another routine for a value and returns only its lowest bit.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:853E
name: mask_result_low_two_bits
description: Calls another routine for a value and returns its two lowest bits.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8548
name: mask_result_low_three_bits
description: Calls another routine for a value and returns its three lowest bits.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8552
name: mask_result_low_six_bits
description: Calls another routine for a value and returns its six lowest bits.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:855C
name: forward_result_byte
description: Calls another routine and returns its result as a byte.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8566
name: modulo_result_by_argument
description: Calls another routine and returns the remainder of its low 16 bits divided by the low 16 bits of the argument. The remainder is placed in the upper word of the result, with the argument in the lower word.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:857A
name: call_then_library_vector_60
description: Calls another routine, then calls a library vector at a fixed offset from the library base stored in a global slot. It returns the D0 and D1 register values unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:85A6
name: format_decimal_right_aligned
description: Writes the value in D0 as decimal digits into a text buffer, starting at the right end and moving left until the value reaches zero. It fills the remaining positions on the left with spaces.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:85AE
name: format_decimal_fixed_width
description: Writes a value as decimal digits into a field whose width is given in D1, filling from the right. Once the value reaches zero it pads the remaining positions on the left with spaces.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:85CA
name: fill_spaces_from_index
description: Writes space characters into a buffer from the index in D1 down to zero.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:85F6
name: run_nested_callback_loops
description: Counts down through three nested loops, calling a routine from a function-pointer table on each pass. An extra group of calls runs while the outer counter is above nine. It returns the input registers unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:86FA
name: print_text_segments
description: Walks a zero-terminated string. A byte with only its top bit set triggers a call to another routine; any other run of characters is measured and passed to a library vector at a fixed offset together with its length.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:874E
name: lookup_tile_attribute_nibble
description: Computes a tile position from two coordinate arguments, clamped against stored offsets, and looks up a map byte and then a flag table entry. It returns the upper nibble of the attribute byte when a mask chosen from argument bits is set, and zero otherwise.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8756
name: lookup_tile_attribute_nibble_regs
description: Register-argument variant of the tile attribute lookup. It performs the same mask, clamp, map and flag table calculation using the D0 and D1 register values, and returns the upper nibble when the mask bit is set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:87EE
name: call_library_vector_42_decrement
description: Calls a library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot, then subtracts four from a stored counter.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8810
name: call_library_vector_42_adjust
description: Calls a library vector at a fixed offset from a library base stored in a global slot, then subtracts a value derived from a stored pointer plus four from a stored counter.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8838
name: call_routine_sequence_with_global
description: Calls another routine once with a value from a global slot, then calls the routine many more times in succession with no arguments. It returns the input registers unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:88F0
name: call_routine_six_times
description: Calls another routine six times in succession and returns.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:890A
name: copy_block_to_multiple_buffers
description: Copies 16-bit words from a source block into five destination buffers, moving two words per buffer on each of sixteen iterations with a fixed stride between destinations.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8964
name: stub_return_only
description: Routine consisting only of a return; the listing shows no calls, memory access or register use.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:896E
name: call_global_arg_return_regs
description: Calls another routine with a value from a global slot and returns the input register values unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:89C8
name: call_routine_run_with_global
description: Calls another routine with a value from a global slot, then calls the same routine many more times with no arguments. It returns the input registers unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8A62
name: forward_call_once
description: Calls another routine once and returns. It manipulates no data itself.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8A70
name: iterate_map_cell_grid
description: Clamps two coordinates to fixed limits, then loops over nine rows and eighteen columns. For each cell it calls another routine with an address computed from a map byte and the cell offset.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8B30
name: convert_chunky_pixels_to_bitplanes
description: Converts indexed pixel bytes into five planar bit words. Each pixel byte indexes a table whose bits are shifted one per plane into the words, and each finished word is written to its bitplane and to a second row in that plane. It processes eight rows of sixteen pixels.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8BC8
name: copy_word_block_to_bitmap
description: Copies a block of eight rows, each holding four 16-bit words, from a source buffer into a destination bitmap. The destination offset comes from the position arguments and a row stride computed from the bitmap width.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8C18
name: compute_tile_image_address
description: Converts a position into map coordinates relative to a stored origin and clamps them. It reads a map byte at those coordinates, then returns an address formed from that byte, the low bits of the position and a stored base address.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8C84
name: fill_tile_window_buffer
description: Fills a buffer of nineteen rows and six columns with values read from a tile map, using position-derived coordinates. It then stores one further map cell value in a global, adding an offset when a state value is high, and returns both input arguments unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8D48
name: decode_run_length_stream
description: When a flag byte is set, decodes a run-length stream into the output buffer until a stored count is reached: a negative count repeats the next byte, while a positive count copies that many bytes. Otherwise it copies a block of the stored length from the source pointer and advances that pointer.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8DC4
name: scale_value_by_table
description: When the second argument's low byte is below eight, multiplies the third argument by a word from a global table indexed by that byte, halves the product, adds it to the first argument and masks the result to fifteen bits. Otherwise it returns the first argument unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8DEE
name: scale_value_with_sign
description: When the second argument's low byte is below eight, adds half of the third argument times a global table word to the low fifteen bits of the first argument and keeps its sign bit. Otherwise it returns the first argument unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8E20
name: copy_bit14_to_sign_bit
description: Sets bit fifteen of the argument when bit fourteen is set, otherwise clears bit fifteen, and returns the value.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8E30
name: mask_low_fifteen_bits
description: Returns the value in D0 masked to its lower fifteen bits.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8E36
name: follow_target_position
description: Moves a stored x and y position toward target coordinates on each call. It snaps to a fixed offset from the target when the difference is large and steps by one when the difference exceeds a small threshold.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8E6E
name: step_position_from_deltas
description: Adjusts a stored x and y position from delta values in registers D2 and D3. X is stepped by one or reset from the first input when the delta is large, and Y is stepped by one or set from the second input, using the same thresholds.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8E7E
name: step_position_without_x_snap
description: Steps a stored x position by one when delta D2 exceeds the threshold, without any snap. It adjusts the stored y position from delta D3 with the same snap-and-step rules as its neighbours.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8E8A
name: step_x_and_adjust_y
description: Increments a stored x position when delta D2 exceeds twenty, and adjusts the stored y position from delta D3 with the same snap-and-step thresholds as its neighbours.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8EA4
name: adjust_y_position_from_delta
description: Adjusts the stored y position from delta D3. It sets y to the second input minus 44 when the delta is 45 or more, and otherwise steps y by one when the delta magnitude exceeds ten.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8EB4
name: step_y_by_delta_threshold
description: Steps the stored y position down by one when delta D3 is below minus ten, or up by one when it is above ten.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8EC0
name: increment_y_when_delta_positive
description: Increments the stored y position by one when delta D3 exceeds ten.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8ED6
name: report_error_when_not_two
description: When the argument is not two, calls three routines with constant arguments, a global pointer and the argument. The listing references the text ERROR and calls library vectors.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8F0E
name: select_value_by_range_checks
description: Reads an initial byte from a table indexed by the argument. For arguments above ten, a chain of range checks overrides it with a value between three and ten, and the result is returned together with the second register.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8F5A
name: read_joystick_direction_value
description: Decodes the movement bits of the joystick port 1 data register into a direction index. It stores the index and calls another routine when it changes; when the input is centred it decrements a counter. When a flag bit is set, it chooses a value from thresholds applied to two stored coordinates.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8F6E
name: read_joystick_direction_value
description: Decodes the movement bits of the joystick port 1 data register into a direction index. It stores the index and calls another routine when it changes; when the input is centred it decrements a counter. When a flag bit is set, it chooses a value from thresholds applied to two stored coordinates.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:8FC0
name: read_joystick_direction_index
description: Decodes the movement bits of the joystick port 1 data register into a direction index, and stores it and calls another routine when it changes. When the input is centred it decrements a counter.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9012
name: clamp_level_and_notify
description: Subtracts twenty from a stored value. When the result is outside zero to nine it uses nine and resets the stored value to zero; when the level then differs from the previous stored level, it calls another routine with it.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9026
name: set_level_nine_and_notify
description: Resets a stored counter to zero and, when the stored level is not nine, sets it to nine and calls another routine with nine.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9044
name: check_two_results_thresholds
description: Calls another routine and, when its short result is not one and is below ten, calls it again. If the second result is not one and is below eight, it returns zero; otherwise it returns the most recent result.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9080
name: compute_inverted_plane_and
description: Loops over rows of words, writing to the destination the bitwise NOT of the AND of five source words taken from five rows spaced by a stride. The row count comes from the fifth argument.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9112
name: program_blitter_five_entries
description: Takes ownership of the blitter. For each of five entries it waits for the blitter when it is busy, then programs its control, mask, source, destination and size registers from stored values, and finally releases the blitter.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:91A2
name: set_blitter_regs
description: Writes fixed control values to three blitter registers, then stores the first argument in the destination pointer register and the second argument in the size register. It returns zero.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:91CC
name: program_blitter_five_planes_masked
description: For each of five entries, waits for the blitter when it is busy, then sets its control, mask, source, destination and modulo registers from stored values with a shift-derived mask, and stores the computed pointers.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9286
name: program_blitter_single_entry
description: Programs the blitter for one copy without a loop. It waits for the blitter when it is busy, then sets its control, mask, pointer, modulo and size values from stored fields.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9310
name: program_blitter_five_steps_dest
description: For each of five entries, waits for the blitter when it is busy, then sets its control value, masks and pointers from stored fields. The argument is added to the stepped value stored in the destination pointer register.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9390
name: program_blitter_five_steps_src
description: For each of five entries, waits for the blitter when it is busy, then sets its control value, masks and pointers from stored fields. The argument is added to the stepped value stored in the source pointer register.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9414
name: call_global_pointer_no_args
description: Calls the routine whose address is stored in a fixed global slot, with no arguments, and returns.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:94F2
name: call_second_global_pointer
description: Calls the routine whose address is stored in a second fixed global slot, with no arguments, and returns.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9BEC
name: compute_direction_toward_entry
description: Computes signed x and y differences from a stored entry position and converts them to direction signs. It looks up a direction code in a table, then stores an adjusted direction in the entry, or sets another field for a special code. It returns the input registers with the low three bits set.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9BF6
name: compute_direction_toward_entry_plain
description: Computes signed x and y differences from a stored entry position and converts them to direction signs. It looks up a direction code in a table, then stores an adjusted direction in the entry, or sets another field for a special code. It returns the input registers unchanged.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9C32
name: store_direction_from_signs
description: Negates a sign value depending on a status bit from another routine, adds it to a direction value, and stores the sum masked to three bits in the entry. It sets a field to twelve unless the mode argument is five.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9C40
name: store_direction_signs_mode
description: Computes sign flags from two coordinate differences and a mode value, looks up a direction code in a table and stores it in the entry masked to three bits when the code is not special. It sets a field to twelve unless the mode is five.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9CAA
name: store_adjusted_direction
description: Calls another routine and negates a direction value when a status bit is clear, then stores the sum of two direction values masked to three bits in the entry. It sets a field to twelve unless the mode is five.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9CB8
name: store_byte_difference
description: Stores the masked difference of two register bytes into the entry's direction byte, and sets the next byte to twelve unless the mode is five.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9CD4
name: update_entry_timer_and_target
description: Subtracts a step from a record's timer and clamps it at zero. It then chooses a new target from branches set by the arguments, calling other routines, and runs follow-up checks that may call another routine. A first state check passing leads to a recursive call with a fixed code.

key: faery tale adventure, the (1986)(microillusions)[a5]/Faery Tale Adventure, The (1986)(MicroIllusions)[a5].adf:FMAIN:0:9D3A
name: update_timer_and_target_alt
description: Variant of the entry timer update. It subtracts the step from the record's timer, clamps it at zero, chooses a new target from argument-dependent branches, and then runs the follow-up checks.
